long_biography.plain_text:
At twelve, Lars Thrane built a radio transmitter. He later studied engineering at the Technical University of Denmark and completed a doctorate. In 1981, he and his twin brother Per launched a company for which their father Erland became chairman. Lars concentrated on turning advances in radio and satellite technology into marketable communications systems. The enterprise grew internationally before its acquisition by Cobham ended his leadership there.

Thrane returned to product development in 2014 with Lars Thrane A/S. Based in Holte, it designs Iridium-based communications and navigation devices for commercial fleets and leisure craft. Danish registry records name him chairman, while day-to-day management lies with other executives.
